title: Class-Conditional Conformal Prediction with Uncertainty-Triggered Selective Explainability for HighStakes Imbalanced Tabular Decisions
abstract: Abstract: Machine learning models deployed in high-stakes clinical and financial decision-making conventionally output uncalibrated point predictions and soft probabilities that exhibit unwarranted overconfidence. When applied to severely imbalanced tabular distributions—such as acute stroke events or rare cardiovascular disorders—traditional classification objectives incentivize models to minimize global risk by predicting the dominant majority class, inducing near-total sensitivity collapse on critical minority instances. While Conformal Prediction (CP) provides distribution-free finite-sample guarantees, standard marginal calibration suffers from an overlooked failure mode: it achieves nominal marginal coverage globally by over-covering the majority class while catastrophically under-covering the rare disease class (collapsing to coverage on stroke events). To resolve this safety-critical vulnerability, we introduce the Adaptive Penalized Class-Conditional Conformal Predictor (AP-CCCP), a mathematically rigorous framework establishing finite-sample class-conditional guarantees conditioned on exchangeability. AP-CCCP formulates a regularized non-conformity metric integrating an adaptive rarity penalty with margin epistemic uncertainty. Furthermore, we design an Uncertainty-Triggered Selective Explainability protocol that utilizes conformal set cardinality as an autonomous triage trigger: unambiguous singleton predictions () receive an automated fast-pass, whereas borderline or ambiguous cases () trigger on-demand TreeSHAP attribution maps. We benchmark across three clinical cohorts (Kaggle Stroke with 1:20 imbalance, Framingham Heart Study with 1:5.6 imbalance, and Pima Diabetes with 1:1.9 imbalance) and four heterogeneous model families (LightGBM, XGBoost, Random Forest, Deep MLP) across 120 stratified cross-validation folds. While Standard Split CP omits of true stroke cases, AP-CCCP rigorously secures rare-class coverage while reducing post-hoc explainability computational overhead by with automated triage precision up to . This establishes a robust foundation for trustworthy and computationally efficient tabular decision systems. Keywords: Conformal Prediction, Class Imbalance, Finite-Sample Guarantees, Explainable AI (XAI), Selective SHAP, Clinical Decision Support, Tabular Deep Learning, Uncertainty Quantification

title: 基于自适应的动态优化变量选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic optimization variable selection method based on adaptive algorithms. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle complex data and varying input characteristics. This work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts the weights of optimization variables during the optimization process, enhancing the data's adaptability and ultimately improving optimization results. The core mechanism involves a self-adjusting algorithm that adapts to the data's characteristics and the optimization's progress, resulting in more accurate and efficient solutions. The proposed method offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, particularly in scenarios requiring robust and adaptable optimization.

title: Cognitive Graph Representation for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to machine learning utilizing Cognitive Graph Representation (CGR). CGR fundamentally shifts the paradigm by modeling knowledge and relationships within machine learning models as cognitive graphs. These graphs explicitly incorporate uncertainty, inference chains, and metacognitive processes, leading to significant improvements in learning efficiency and generalization performance. The core of CGR lies in a graph structure where nodes represent concepts and edges represent relationships, each associated with a confidence score and a set of inference rules. The model actively navigates this graph, dynamically seeking connections and refining its understanding through a process mirroring human cognition. We argue that this integration of cognitive science principles directly into the architecture of machine learning models represents a crucial step towards creating more robust, adaptable, and explainable AI systems. The theoretical framework and underlying mechanisms are presented, highlighting the potential advantages of CGR over traditional representation learning techniques. The key contribution is the development of a systematic approach to constructing and utilizing cognitive graphs for machine learning applications.

abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for constructing knowledge graphs utilizing graph neural networks (GNNs) to enable dynamic adaptation of knowledge graph structures and content. Traditional knowledge graph construction methods often lack adaptability to evolving data and user behavior. This work introduces a GNN-based adaptive knowledge graph building process, which dynamically adjusts the graph's structure and content based on real-time data and user interactions. The proposed framework significantly enhances knowledge graph accuracy and interpretability compared to static approaches. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on a benchmark dataset.

title: Quantum Error Mitigation via Entanglement Suppression
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is a crucial area of research for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computation. While various QEM techniques have been developed, many rely on classical post-processing of quantum measurements, which can introduce their own biases and limitations. This paper proposes a novel hardware error mitigation strategy leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement and its susceptibility to environmental decoherence. The core idea is to actively suppress quantum decoherence, specifically targeting the entanglement that contributes significantly to error propagation in quantum computations. We formulate a control scheme that precisely modulates environmental parameters to minimize the detrimental effects of entanglement-induced decoherence. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis, outlining the potential for significant error reduction without relying on complex post-processing algorithms. The key benefit lies in a proactive, hardware-level approach to mitigating errors, offering a potentially more robust and efficient solution compared to post-processing methods. This work establishes a foundational framework for future research in entanglement-aware QEM.

title: Title: Geometric Topology for Quantum Simulation of Superposition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for simulating quantum superposition leveraging geometric topology. Traditional quantum simulation methods often struggle with computational complexity, particularly when dealing with complex quantum states. We propose a method that represents quantum states as geometric objects, utilizing topology to capture the essential relationships between them. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and elegant solution to the simulation challenge, paving the way for more sophisticated quantum computations. Geometry offers a powerful and adaptable tool for exploring the intricacies of quantum mechanics.

title: Title: Geometric Proof of Intuitive Probability: Applying Constraint-Based Reasoning to Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging geometric reasoning to provide a rigorous foundation for probability and Bayesian inference. Traditional probability models often rely on approximations and assumptions, prompting a search for a more fundamental and provable framework. We propose a novel approach that formalizes probability as a geometric concept, utilizing a "Constraint Space" – a space defined by geometric relationships. This space serves as a proof system, allowing us to rigorously prove the existence of certain probabilistic events. The core mechanism centers around establishing the validity of probabilistic statements through geometric transformations and constraints, offering a potentially more robust and fundamental approach compared to existing statistical methods. This work will demonstrate the feasibility of this geometric proof system and explore its implications for Bayesian inference.

title: Dynamic Topological Field Theory Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Dynamic Topological Field Theory (DTFT) optimization techniques to complex topological structures. We propose a novel optimization algorithm predicated on the inherent properties of DTFT, aiming to efficiently locate optimal solutions within challenging topological landscapes. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the topology of the search space to guide the search, offering a potentially more effective approach compared to traditional optimization methods. The paper details the theoretical foundations of DTFT, outlines the proposed algorithm's design and implementation, and discusses the potential benefits and limitations of this approach. The work explores how DTFT's inherent structure can be exploited to accelerate the search and improve the convergence of optimization algorithms.

title: Quantum Information Geometry
abstract: Quantum Information Geometry (QIG) proposes a novel framework integrating quantum information theory with geometric analysis, positioning quantum states as fundamental building blocks for understanding quantum entanglement and quantum computation. This paper explores a new approach to leveraging the geometric properties of quantum states to unlock deeper insights into the complexities of quantum mechanics. We introduce a conceptual model centered around the concept of "geometric entanglement," where entanglement isn't just a correlation but a geometric phenomenon inherent in the quantum state. The core mechanism involves developing quantum geometry algorithms to analyze and manipulate these geometric properties, ultimately aiming to provide a more intuitive and mathematically rigorous understanding of quantum information. The paper then highlights the significance of this approach, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize quantum algorithm design and the exploration of quantum information's underlying structure.

title: A hierarchical pipeline for preprocessing and classification of breast histopathology images into benign and malignant
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of death among women across the world. Currently, healthcare informatics is primarily centered on classifying breast cancer images, given the life-threatening nature of this disease. However, variations between and within observers can occur, which may result in misdiagnosis during cancer detection. The proposed work contains a framework for enhancement, segmentation of nuclei followed by classification of breast histopathological images. Enhancement is performed using gaussian filter and decorrelation stretch methods. Segmentation of nuclei is accomplished by extracting YCbCr components, enhancing Y component using Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and applying K-means clustering technique. K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers are employed for automatic classification of breast histopathological images based on texture, geometry and YCbCr features. The proposed method is tested on publicly available BreakHis dataset and yielded best enhancement results for gaussian filter with highest PSNR and lowest RMSE values. The classifiers were assessed using performance metrics including accuracy, specificity, sensitivity and F-score. Experimental results revealed that the SVM achieved better performance than the existing methods, attaining nearly 87.5% accuracy on the dataset.

title: Search-to-World: Evaluation of 3D World Delivery from User Request through Web Search
abstract: Agentic systems can interpret user requests, search the live web, and use external tools, but their ability to transform retrieved web content into a usable 3D world has not been systematically evaluated. No established end-to-end pipeline or benchmark exists for this capability. We introduce Search-to-World, an end-to-end evaluation task covering request understanding, web visual-content retrieval, and 3D-world delivery. We define Observed Retrieval Rate (ORR) and World Delivery Rate (WDR) to distinguish observing relevant content from successfully delivering a request-aligned, perceptually acceptable world. We also present WorldSearcher, a reuse-then-reconstruction harness that connects existing search agents to world delivery: it first retrieves reusable 3D worlds and, when none are available, reconstructs a world from video. A structured recovery controller revises temporal grounding, replaces source videos, or reformulates queries after failure. Using WorldSearcher, we benchmark representative models on Search-to-World and study supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for recovery subagents. Results show that delivery depends on the underlying agentic model, and that relevant-content observation does not ensure world delivery. Jointly training recovery agents improves delivery success and action efficiency. Search-to-World makes agentic 3D-world delivery measurable, while WorldSearcher provides a practical evaluation harness with recovery capabilities.

title: Probing the Structure and Dynamics of LLM Value Expression through Value Conflicts
abstract: Ethical evaluation of Large Language Models (LLMs) often characterizes model values as static and monolithic. In contrast, we argue that LLM value expression is better understood as a structured yet dynamic phenomenon. To investigate this, we introduce Conflict-driven Value Probing, a controlled framework that places LLMs in value conflicts and implements four types of interventions that perturb these conflicts to probe LLM value expression. Applying this framework to ten LLMs, we identify three recurring patterns. (1) Expression duality: models shift from broad idealistic orientations in abstract assessment toward more pragmatic priorities in concrete conflicts. (2) Functional steerability: models readily reconfigure their expressed value profiles toward task-defined value objectives. (3) Bounded plasticity: such reconfiguration is not without constraints, i.e. pressure induces a security- and goal-oriented priority shift while negative framing distinguishes protected values from those more amenable to redirection. Together, these findings characterize both the structure and dynamics of LLM value expression: context flexibly reconfigures expressed priorities, yet within behavioral boundaries. This behavioral account provides a foundation for understanding controllability, alignment, and safety in LLMs. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ZeroGen-Lab/CFProbe.

title: lean-misc-math: miscellaneous mathematical results formalised in Lean 4
abstract: A Lean 4 library of miscellaneous classical and other mathematical results built on Mathlib. This repository is the product of two different kinds of work, and the distinction is deliberate. The choice of which results to formalise, how they should be stated and in what generality, and which are worth publishing is the author's contribution, as is a best-effort read of each Lean statement against its informal claim. The Lean statements and their proofs are generated by Claude; the proofs are read by nobody. Both are checked by Lean's kernel and audited so that every declaration depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The consequence worth internalising is that a mistake here will not be a wrong proof, because the kernel does not admit those. It will be a statement that does not say what it appears to say. A best-effort read is not a review: one person, no second reader, and no reading of the proof. Every result therefore ships an informal statement, a source, a provenance record and sanity checks, including a satisfiability witness for every hypothesis, so that a reader can check the correspondence in about thirty seconds without reading a proof. Users should verify that a statement says what they need before relying on it. The selection and curation of results is the contribution being credited by a citation.

title: 基于多模态协同推理的知识图谱嵌入
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge graph embedding that leverages multi-modal collaborative reasoning. Existing knowledge graph embedding methods often rely solely on textual information, limiting their ability to capture the rich semantic nuances present in real-world knowledge. Our proposed method addresses this limitation by integrating diverse data modalities – including text, images, and audio – through a multi-modal attention mechanism combined with logical reasoning rules. This allows us to generate more comprehensive and contextually relevant embeddings for knowledge graph entities. The core claim is that collaborative reasoning across multiple modalities significantly enhances the quality of knowledge graph embeddings. The core mechanism involves learning relationships between different modalities using multi-modal attention and integrating logical inference rules to construct multi-modal knowledge graph embeddings. We demonstrate that our approach surpasses the limitations of single-modality knowledge graphs, significantly improving knowledge representation and reasoning capabilities.

title: Relational Reinforcement Learning with Knowledge Graph Integration
abstract: Relational Reinforcement Learning (RRL) aims to address the challenges posed by environments where actions influence the state, creating complex dependencies between states. However, traditional RRL methods often struggle to scale effectively, particularly in environments with intricate relational structures. This paper introduces a novel approach to RRL that integrates a knowledge graph (KG) to augment the agent's understanding of the environment. The KG represents the relationships between states and actions, providing prior knowledge and guiding the agent's exploration process. We formalize this approach using a modified Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework, incorporating the KG as a structured memory. The key idea is to leverage the KG's inherent relational information to reduce the search space and accelerate learning. We propose a learning algorithm that utilizes graph traversal techniques to sample relevant states and actions, effectively exploiting the KG's connectivity. The core claim is that integrating a KG significantly improves the scalability of RRL. The mechanism relies on providing the agent with a structured representation of the environment, enabling more efficient exploration and decision-making. Experimental results, though not presented here due to the nature of this theoretical exploration, demonstrate the potential of this approach. The paper concludes with directions for future research and potential applications.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Optimization Strategies
abstract: Quantum topology, a relatively recent field of physics, offers a unique approach to designing quantum systems. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum topology to develop adaptive optimization strategies for quantum computation. We propose a novel framework that leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters, enabling efficient and potentially transformative quantum algorithms. The core of this approach lies in a mechanism that allows the system to self-correct and adapt its behavior in response to changing conditions. The paper details the proposed framework, its mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. We highlight the advantages over traditional optimization methods, emphasizing the potential for improved performance and scalability.

title: Information Entropy-Driven Distributed Learning (IEDDL)
abstract: This paper introduces Information Entropy-Driven Distributed Learning (IEDDL), a novel approach to distributed learning that leverages the concept of information entropy to guide convergence and optimize global optimality. The core claim is that by explicitly incorporating entropy measures, we can significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of distributed learning algorithms. The proposed mechanism involves a distributed learning algorithm dynamically adjusting learning rates and parameters based on the entropy differences between nodes. This approach aims to accelerate convergence and enhance the likelihood of achieving global optima. We present a detailed formulation of the IEDDL algorithm, focusing on the mathematical principles underlying its operation. The primary contribution lies in the novel application of entropy as a steering force within the distributed learning process, addressing prevalent convergence challenges often encountered in traditional distributed learning methods. We explore theoretical implications and provide a framework for future research in this area. ---

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, but it frequently operates under the assumption of a deterministic environment. This simplification ignores a crucial aspect of real-world scenarios – inherent uncertainty. This work proposes a novel approach to RL by integrating probabilistic programming, enabling the explicit modeling and learning of uncertainty. The core idea is to utilize a probabilistic programming language to represent the environment's dynamics, allowing the agent to learn policies that are inherently robust to noise and stochastic variations. We demonstrate that this approach leads to improved performance and stability, particularly in environments characterized by significant uncertainty. The methodology introduces a framework for incorporating prior knowledge about the environment and dynamically updating this knowledge during learning. We formalize this framework using probabilistic models and present a methodology for learning optimal policies within this framework. This paper outlines the key components of this approach, focusing on the mathematical foundations and the design of the learning algorithm. The results presented highlight the potential of probabilistic programming to revolutionize RL, moving beyond deterministic assumptions and fostering more reliable and adaptable agents.

title: 基于量子自适应的机器学习框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-enhanced machine learning framework, termed "Quantum Adaptive Machine Learning" (QAML), leveraging quantum self-adaptation to enhance the performance of various machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning often struggles with complex, high-dimensional data, requiring extensive parameter tuning. QAML addresses this challenge by employing quantum self-adaptation, a quantum mechanical phenomenon allowing the system to dynamically adjust its parameters based on the data itself. We detail the framework's architecture, explain the core mechanisms driving its enhanced performance, and provide a comparative analysis with existing techniques. The study demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency across several benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of this approach for tackling complex machine learning tasks.

title: Explainable AI through Counterfactual Explanation Generation with Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is a critical area of research, aiming to make AI systems more transparent and understandable to humans. However, many existing XAI techniques struggle to provide truly insightful explanations, often relying on superficial correlations rather than a fundamental understanding of the underlying causal mechanisms driving model decisions. This paper introduces a novel approach to XAI that leverages Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to generate counterfactual explanations. These explanations, framed as "what if" scenarios, are grounded in causal relationships, offering a more robust and interpretable understanding of model behavior. The core idea is to construct CBNs representing the relationships between input features and model outputs, and then use these networks to identify minimal changes to the input that would lead to a different output. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, highlighting its ability to produce explanations that align with causal understanding, addressing a key limitation of current XAI methods. The generated counterfactuals are not merely spurious correlations but reflect the true causal influences on the model's predictions. This approach has significant implications for building trust in AI systems and facilitating informed decision-making.

evidence.title: Explainable AI through Counterfactual Explanation Generation with Causal Bayesian Networks
evidence.abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is a critical area of research, aiming to make AI systems more transparent and understandable to humans. However, many existing XAI techniques struggle to provide truly insightful explanations, often relying on superficial correlations rather than a fundamental understanding of the underlying causal mechanisms driving model decisions. This paper introduces a novel approach to XAI that leverages Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) to generate counterfactual explanations. These explanations, framed as "what if" scenarios, are grounded in causal relationships, offering a more robust and interpretable understanding of model behavior. The core idea is to construct CBNs representing the relationships between input features and model outputs, and then use these networks to identify minimal changes to the input that would lead to a different output. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, highlighting its ability to produce explanations that align with causal understanding, addressing a key limitation of current XAI methods. The generated counterfactuals are not merely spurious correlations but reflect the true causal influences on the model's predictions. This approach has significant implications for building trust in AI systems and facilitating informed decision-making.

title: The Adaptive Matrix Transformation of Non-Linear Gradient Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning model training leveraging adaptive matrix transformation and non-linear gradient enhancement. The core idea centers on dynamically adjusting transformation parameters during training to enhance model generalization and reduce overfitting. We detail the algorithm's design, incorporating a self-adaptive matrix transformation process, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations and analysis. The research focuses on improving the robustness and accuracy of machine learning models, specifically in scenarios where overfitting is a significant concern.

title: Dynamic Probability Distributions: Mathematical Modeling and Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic probability distributions as a complex system for optimization, leveraging a novel approach to parameter adjustment based on a probabilistic window. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts the parameters of a Gaussian distribution to optimize a target function, effectively mimicking the behavior of complex systems. The core mechanism involves defining a probabilistic window, allowing the distribution to adapt to environmental changes. This adaptation is achieved through iterative parameter adjustments based on a feedback loop, ensuring a continuously optimized outcome. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through numerical simulations and a detailed analysis of its performance across various objective functions. The goal is to provide a robust and adaptable method for optimization, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic and unpredictable environments.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive machine learning optimization algorithm designed to address the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The algorithm dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on input data, enabling it to efficiently navigate complex and high-dimensional datasets. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the performance of the optimization process and adapts the parameters accordingly. This adaptive approach significantly enhances optimization efficiency and robustness compared to static optimization techniques. The paper details the algorithm's design, the rationale behind its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness on a diverse set of benchmark problems.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Lattice-Based Simulations
abstract: Quantum-enhanced lattice-based simulations represent a significant advancement in materials design and computational modeling, offering the potential to dramatically accelerate the discovery of novel materials with tailored properties. This paper explores a novel approach to lattice simulations leveraging quantum computing to enhance accuracy and computational efficiency. We introduce a new quantum algorithm designed to address the limitations of classical methods, specifically focusing on the intricate interplay of many-body interactions within complex lattice structures. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum algorithms to directly explore the potential energy landscape of the system, leading to a more precise and efficient representation of material behavior. This paper presents a detailed overview of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential to revolutionize materials science.

title: Zero-Shot Evaluation of Multilingual Models for Bidirectional English–Indic Machine Translation
abstract: The recent outbreak of Large Language Models~(LLMs) has radically changed the state of machine translation~(MT), which has provided fresh possibilities to low-resource and morphologically rich language pairs. The paper is a detailed comparative analysis of five state-of-the-art models, BLOOMZ, IndicTrans2, Krutrim, Sarvam~AI, and Aya-101, in a zero-shot translation paradigm between English and four typologically different languages, Indic languages: Gujarati, Malayalam, Hindi, and Tamil. The analysis compares general-purpose multilingual LLMs to specialised neural machine translation systems (NMT) in a systematic way balancing the generality of multilingual coverage and task specialisation. Every model is tested on the FLORES-200 DevTest corpus against three complementary testing metrics, BLEU, chrF++ and COMET. The languages selected represent two different linguistic families, that is, Indo-Aryan (Hindi, Gujarati) and Dravidian (Tamil, Malayalam), which gives them a principled ground of cross-family comparison. Experimentation findings indicate that there is significant performance difference among language pairs, translation directions and models. Specialised Indic models are proven to have marked morphologically rich languages of Dravidian language families on both semantic and character-level measures, LLM instruction-tuned models are also shown to achieve good performance in limited resources environments with respect to BLEU. The results of our work provide practical recommendations in the selection of LLM in the production Indic MT pipeline and emphasize the importance of the linguistic family factor in the assessment of the multilingual model.

title: Revisiting noise in learning: A generalized fractional Tikhonov approach within the adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system for classification problems
abstract: In machine learning, noise has traditionally been regarded as a detrimental factor. However, recent studies have revealed its potential to enhance learning through mechanisms such as noise-induced regularization and data augmentation. Building upon the established connection between input noise injection and Tikhonov regularization, this study proposes a generalized fractional Tikhonov regularization within the Adaptive Network-Based Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) framework. We introduce a novel model, ANFIS-GT, generalizing the previous ANFIS-T scheme, which has been the first ANFIS variant equipped with fractional Tikhonov regularization, in order to improve its classification performance. The proposed method employs differential quadrature rules to construct the regularization matrix in the penalty term, extending the conventional fractional Tikhonov approach that assumes an identity matrix. We formally prove the error stability of the new scheme, establishing a result that also holds for the former ANFIS-T under certain conditions, for which stability had not previously been demonstrated. Furthermore, we analytically identify the conditions under which the solution of the proposed scheme is equivalent to that obtained by small perturbations of the system’s input in a non-penalized error function. Extensive evaluations on binary and multiclass classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, validating the theoretical developments and yielding a robust, interpretable, and effective learning model.

title: Disentangling decoder capacity and directionality in type constrained knowledge graph link prediction
abstract: Decoder comparisons in typed knowledge graph (KG) link prediction often confound relation specificity, off-diagonal interactions, and directionality. We separate these factors with four seed-matched decoders applied to GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT encoders: a shared inner product (IP), a relation-specific diagonal bilinear decoder (RD), a symmetric full bilinear decoder (SB), and an unconstrained directed bilinear decoder (D). The study uses a regulation-grounded coal-mine safety KG with 5,093 nodes and 19,314 canonical directed edges. All 120 decoder–encoder–seed cells use the same ten non-adjacent seeds, type-constrained splits, fixed negatives, and training budget. Two-sided paired AUC tests use pre-specified Holm families, with full filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10 reported descriptively. RD produced no detectable AUC improvement over IP for any of the three encoders under the matched ten-seed design. SB improved on RD for GraphSAGE ( $$\bf{\Delta}$$ AUC $$\bf{=0.0254}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=2.15\times10^{-5}}$$ ) and GAT ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.1667}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=3.24\times10^{-10}}$$ ), but not GCN. Releasing the SB symmetry constraint and enlarging the direction-sensitive score space (D $$-$$ SB) increased AUC for GCN ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.0423}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=4.77\times10^{-5}}$$ ) and GraphSAGE ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.0116}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=0.00251}$$ ), whereas the GAT contrast was not detected. Thus, no RD-over-IP improvement was detected, while the contributions of symmetric off-diagonal interaction and of releasing symmetry while enlarging the direction-sensitive score space depend on the encoder. A deterministic semantic hard-negative stress test, all-family filtered ranking, and a frozen-embedding symmetric/skew diagnostic support but do not enter the confirmatory tests. Candidate discovery uses threshold-free top-five within-family ranking. These results support a narrow conclusion: decoder function class matters in this typed transductive setting, but no decoder is universally superior.

title: Bottom-up Modeling of Repeated Elements via Single Image Analysis-by-Synthesis
abstract: We address the problem of discovering repeated elements from a single image. In contrast to existing approaches that depend on large annotated datasets, curated multi-image collections, or object segmentation masks, we show that a single image can suffice to learn a meaningful object model in a completely bottom-up fashion, without any prior knowledge beyond a coarse scale prior. Our method learns a tunable image-space prototype of the repeated elements through a reconstruction objective, enabling the model to identify and synthesize consistent object instances within the same image. Experiments on 116 real images from the FSC-147 dataset demonstrate that our method successfully learns coherent element models and captures intra-category variation on challenging images. Qualitative results reveal superior reconstructions and interpretable decompositions compared to classical decomposition, joint alignment, and 3D object modeling methods, while maintaining a simple 2D formulation. These results suggest that meaningful object discovery can emerge from single image learning alone.

title: Constitutive State-Space Modeling of Path-Dependent Plasticity: A Resolution-Consistent and Parallelizable Computational Framework
abstract: Data-driven constitutive models for path-dependent plasticity are commonly formulated using nonlinear recurrent neural networks, whose sequential state evolution limits parallel training and whose predictions may depend on the discretization of the applied strain path. We introduce a Constitutive State Space (CSS) model that reformulates structured state-space dynamics as an incremental constitutive operator. The strain increment is decomposed into magnitude and direction: the loading direction drives the latent state-space system, while the increment magnitude enters the zero-order-hold discretization of its continuous-time linear recurrence. This mechanics-tailored construction guarantees stationarity under zero increments, strongly reduces sensitivity to strain-path resolution, and retains the parallel-scan structure of S5 for efficient training on long constitutive histories. The CSS and Minimal State Cell (MSC) architectures are compared for four multiaxial path-dependent material models including isotropic J2 plasticity, pressure-sensitive foam plasticity, and combined isotropic-kinematic hardening. CSS matches or exceeds the prediction accuracy of the MSC, including one order of magnitude lower validation losses for the plastically incompressible materials. Importantly, CSS maintains low errors across large changes in strain-path discretization, whereas the MSC error increases substantially when evaluated at coarser resolutions than used for training. CSS trains substantially faster and requires fewer strain-stress pairs to attain comparable or better accuracy. Analysis of the learned state further reveals latent structure consistent with the dimensionality of the underlying physical constitutive models. These results establish mechanics-tailored structured state-space dynamics as a computational framework for efficient and discretization-robust data-driven constitutive modeling.

title: ARNAI: Artifact Removal Network based on Autoencoding and Inpainting for Robust Spinal Image Segmentation and Measurement
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop an AI framework applicable for postoperative imaging for automated measurement of spinopelvic parameters on radiographs with robustness to the presence of spinal implants. Materials and Methods: We retrospectively reviewed lateral lumbar spine radiographs from two institutions (Internal: January 2017--December 2024; External: October 2021--September 2025). We developed the Restore, Segment, and Measure (RSM) framework, incorporating a novel Artifact Removal Network based on Autoencoding and Inpainting (ARNAI) to mitigate implant-related artifacts in postoperative radiographs. Segmentation and spinopelvic parameter (PT, LL, SS, SCA) measurement performance were assessed using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and intraclass correlation coefficients. Results: When ARNAI was added to a recent Transformer-based segmentation model, FCBFormer, the mean DSC increased to 0.870 from 0.814, with marked gains at L3--L5 and smaller improvements at L1--L2. On 91 radiographs with implants, the mean L4--L5 segmental Cobb angle error decreased to 4.7 ° from 15.6--16.2 °, an average error reduction of 70%. The ICC for L4--L5 segmental Cobb angle improved to 0.54 (Rater 1) and 0.59 (Rater 2) from 0.18, and ICCs for pelvic tilt, lumbar lordosis, and sacral slope all exceeded 0.70. The improvement in L4--L5 segmental Cobb angle error was statistically significant in the internal implant-containing cohort after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion: The proposed RSM framework improved automated spinopelvic parameter measurement in implant-containing postoperative radiographs. By mitigating implant-related artifacts, ARNAI improved segmentation and downstream measurement accuracy, with the greatest benefit observed for L4--L5 segmental Cobb angle estimation, where the mean error was reduced by approximately 70%.

title: Fixed Versus Fuzzy Self-Tuning PID Speed Control of a Geared DC Motor: Experimental Identification and Robustness Evaluation
abstract: يُعد التحكم التناسبي-التكاملي-التفاضلي (PID) ذو المعاملات الثابتة خياراً جذاباً لمحركات التيار المستمر منخفضة التكلفة، إلا أن أداءه قد يتدهور عند تغير الحمل أو معاملات المنظومة عن شروط الضبط. تقارن هذه الدراسة بين متحكم PID ثابت ومتحكم PID ضبابي ذاتي الضبط من نوع Sugeno من الرتبة الصفرية لتنظيم سرعة محرك JGA25-370 بجهد 12 فولت وعلبة تروس. استُخدم Arduino Uno مع مشغل L298N ومشفّر Hall للحصول على استجابة خطوة في الحلقة المفتوحة بزمن أخذ عينات 100 ms. أسفرت عملية تعريف تعتمد على خطأ الخرج مع مراعاة المرشح عن النموذج من الدرجة الأولى G(s)=10.8826/(0.024254s+1) rpm/V، بخطأ ملاءمة RMS مقداره 0.1553 rpm ومعامل تحديد R²=0.999938. تم تقييم المتحكمين في MATLAB/Simulink تحت افتراضات متماثلة لأخذ العينات والتكميم والترشيح والتشبع ومنع التكامل الزائد. عند 100 rpm حقق المتحكمان زمن صعود 0.4 s، بينما استقر PID الثابت في 0.6 s مقابل 0.8 s للمتحكم الضبابي وحقق مؤشرات خطأ تكاملية أقل. تحت اضطراب مكافئ مقداره 2 V خفّض الضبط الضبابي أقصى انحراف في السرعة بنسبة 26.88% وزمن الاستعادة بنسبة 40% وIAE بعد الحدث بنسبة 51.57%. وتحت تغير المعلمات بلغت التخفيضات المناظرة 28.32% و40% و49.63%. وعبر 500 تجربة Monte Carlo مقترنة انخفض متوسط ITAE وزمن الاستقرار بنسبة 17.94% و13.54% على التوالي، مع زيادة التغير الكلي لإشارة التحكم بمقدار 6.68 مرة. تدعم النتائج استخدام الضبط الضبابي الذاتي كوسيلة لتعزيز المتانة، وليس بديلاً عاماً عن PID ثابت مضبوط جيداً.

title: ClaimBridge: PCT-linked JPO–USPTO claim sets for cross-lingual, multi-jurisdiction patent drafting
abstract: This item contains the dataset and evaluation materials accompanying the following paper:Trung Phuong Le, Hirofumi Nonaka, Koji Marusaki, Katsuhito Sudoh, and Seiya Kawano. 2026. A Large-Scale Dataset for Cross-Lingual Multi-Jurisdiction Patent Drafting from Patent Cooperation Treaty Applications. In Proceedings of the 19th International Natural Language Generation Conference (INLG 2026), Utrecht, the Netherlands. Association for Computational Linguistics.Securing patent protection across countries requires drafting claims separately for each national patent office, in the relevant language and according to its legal and stylistic conventions. Patent claims can therefore differ across languages and jurisdictions because of translation, target-office drafting practice, and prosecution-stage changes. We formulate \emph{cross-lingual patent drafting} as generating plausible candidate claim sets for a specified target language, jurisdiction, and prosecution stage from a source claim set in another language. The task models jurisdiction- and stage-specific transformations beyond content-preserving translation. We construct a large-scale Japanese--English dataset by linking Japan Patent Office (JPO) and United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) records through 884,179 Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)-derived patent families. Across six released configurations, these families yield 4,067,168 directional claim-set instances; four core configurations form the main benchmark. Commercial machine translation and zero- and few-shot prompting capture part of the task, while supervised adaptation provides the strongest overall baseline, showing that task-specific patterns can be learned from linked cross-jurisdictional claim sets.

title: Empirical Validation of Affinity-Aware Steering: Mitigating Degenerative Mode Collapse in Transformer Latent Manifolds via Calibrated Grassmannian Overlap
abstract: Static activation addition injects a fixed steering vector into the residual stream without regard to the instantaneous geometry of the generating trajectory. On long-horizon completions this magnitude-only policy induces representational shear: the hidden state is driven off the local tangent of the token manifold and collapses into a shallow, high-frequency basin of lexical repetition. We test the first empirical gate of the dynamical-spectral architecture—affinity-aware steering—on Qwen2.5-1.5B (hidden dimension d = 1536, 28 layers) intervening at the Layer-14 residual stream. A difference-of-means vector v extracted from five contrastive pairs has Euclidean norm ‖v‖₂ = 21.0469. The target attractor subspace E_A is the leading three-dimensional principal subspace of centered positive activations; the state subspace E_x is a rank-2 delay embedding over a sliding window of width W = 4. Raw Grassmannian overlap in ambient dimension 1536 concentrates near 0.008, statistically indistinguishable from the random-subspace floor 𝔼[‖E_Aᵀ E_x‖_F²] ≈ kr/d = 6/1536 ≈ 0.0039, and therefore suppresses the gating hook. A temperature-scaled sigmoidal transfer, Aff(x_t, A) = σ((Overlap(E_A, E_x) − 0.004) / 0.010) restores usable dynamic range to the interval [0.41, 0.61] (mean 0.526 on the critical prompt). Under greedy decoding, standard ActAdd at coefficient c = 1.8 produces a degenerative loop on Prompt 2 (“Explain how higher-level intelligence organizes chaotic data”), repeating the phrase “hierarchical organization of data” across successive clauses. Calibrated affinity-aware steering abolishes the loop: injection is attenuated during syntactic transitions (affinity ≈ 0.41) and amplified during semantic predicates (affinity ≈ 0.61). The result is a first operational confirmation that subspace-overlap gating, once calibrated against ambient dimensionality, converts a brittle forcing term into a geometry-aware control signal on current residual-stream infrastructure.

title: Hierarchical Fractal Dimension Discovery via Quantum Iteration
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize the discovery of hierarchical fractal dimension properties within data sets. Traditional methods often struggle to capture the intricate complexities of fractal patterns, limiting our ability to accurately characterize data. We propose a novel quantum iteration technique designed to uncover hidden structures and patterns within data, offering a fundamentally different approach to characterization. The core mechanism leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to explore a vast space of potential fractal dimensions, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical computational approaches. This work investigates the feasibility and potential impact of this quantum algorithm on data analysis and characterization. We present a preliminary analysis of the algorithm's potential and outline future research directions.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Chaos, Based on Quantum Simulation of Chaos Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum simulation to the study of non-linear geometric chaos. Traditional chaos theory methods often struggle with the complexities of intricate geometric systems, limiting the ability to accurately model and control their behavior. Quantum simulation offers a novel approach by providing a fundamentally different method for representing and analyzing chaotic dynamics. We propose a new algorithm utilizing quantum simulations to emulate the formation and evolution of complex geometric structures, with the goal of optimizing control strategies through the analysis of simulated chaos. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum simulation to enhance our understanding and control of non-linear geometric chaos.

title: Self-Organized Quantum Topology: A Non-Asymptotic Analysis Approach
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-asymptotic analysis method for investigating the properties and relationships of quantum topology, leveraging the unique self-organizing characteristics of these systems. We propose a framework centered on identifying and quantifying the inherent asymmetries within quantum systems, aiming to uncover potential applications within quantum information science. The core mechanism revolves around the application of quantum topological principles to analyze and understand the fundamental structure of quantum states. This research focuses on identifying novel patterns and relationships that can be discovered through this approach, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum information processing and understanding.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Reasoning about Adversarial Attacks
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose a significant threat to the reliability of machine learning models across a wide range of applications. Current defense strategies often rely on static, deterministic approaches that fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in attacker behavior. This paper proposes a novel framework for defending against adversarial attacks by leveraging probabilistic programming. We represent adversarial attacks as stochastic processes, explicitly modeling their variability and allowing for the development of robust defense strategies. Our approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of attack dynamics and facilitates the design of defenses that are adaptive and resilient to unforeseen attack patterns. We outline the key components of this framework, including the formulation of attack models using probabilistic programming, and demonstrate the potential for improved defense efficacy compared to traditional methods. The core idea is to shift from trying to perfectly predict an attack, to understanding the *probability* of an attack occurring and building defenses that are robust to this probability.

title: Adaptive Neural Networks with Dynamic Neuron Structure Reconfiguration
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design centered around adaptive neuron structure reconfiguration. Traditional neural networks often employ fixed architectures, limiting their adaptability to diverse and evolving learning tasks. We introduce a framework where the network's neuron structure dynamically adjusts itself, aiming to optimize learning efficiency and generalization performance. The core mechanism involves utilizing either a genetic algorithm or reinforcement learning to govern the restructuring process. The system operates on feedback from error signals, iteratively refining the network's topology. This contrasts with existing adaptive networks which primarily focus on weight adjustments. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate the benefits of a more flexible and responsive neural network architecture. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of neuron structure, enabling the network to better capture complex patterns and improve its overall learning capacity. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research in adaptive neural networks and their potential applications.

title: BreastUS-CAD: frozen, pre-registered single-shot external validation of a breast ultrasound benign/malignant classifier, with deployment-oriented follow-up studies and an independent audit trail
abstract: Code, protocols, results and audit trail of BreastUS-CAD; frozen model weights on Hugging Face. Research prototype — not a medical device. A ViT-B/16 classifier trained on the public BUS-BRA dataset with the official patient-level five-fold splits, frozen (git tag frozen-v1) and validated single-shot on four external cohorts (BrEaST, Curated BUSI, GDPH, SYSUCC) under an internally version-controlled pre-registered protocol (data/external_protocol.md + 4 amendments), followed by pre-registered deployment-oriented studies (site-specific recalibration, ensemble-disagreement abstention, domain-pretrained backbone, leave-one-cohort-out multi-source training), an independent adversarial audit (docs/AUDIT_2026-09-06.md), two independent re-audits (docs/AUDIT2_claude_2026-09-11.md, docs/AUDIT2_astra_2026-09-11.md), the item-by-item responses (docs/AUDIT_RESPONSE_2026-09-06.md, docs/AUDIT2_RESPONSE.md), and post-hoc analyses quantifying the disclosed biases. The result tables in RESULTS.md recompute from the committed CSV/JSON artifacts (wandb-derived and latency numbers do not). The internal reference numbers describe one held-out checkpoint per image, not the deployed ensemble. Version 1.1-audited (2026-09-12) supersedes 1.0-audited: corrections per the two re-audits (predictor labelling of the internal reference, the threshold rule as implemented, wording of the post-hoc analyses, false-negative and reader-information statements, provenance statements synchronised after the v1.0 deposition), two new post-hoc analyses, an overwrite guard in the external-validation script, and a self-describing archive (.git-commit holds the archived commit). Erratum for version 1.0-audited: the v1.0 archive's embedded docs/PROVENANCE.md §7, README.md and CITATION.cff describe the archive as commit 1f196a9 with SHA-256 fcd270a5… and "DOI pending"; the deposited file is in fact the archive of commit fa193a8 (verified bit-identical by both re-audits) and those embedded lines predate the tag re-point. Model checkpoints are not in this archive: frozen-v1 weights (repo root) and v2 research checkpoints (v2/) are on Hugging Face with SHA-256 checksums in models/CHECKSUMS.txt. Pre-registration was internal and not externally time-stamped before this deposition; see docs/PROVENANCE.md.

title: Adaptive State Transfer of Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive state transfer of multi-body quantum entanglement, aiming to accelerate the transition between different quantum states. The core concept is leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate rapid and efficient state manipulation. Traditional approaches often rely on static transitions, while this algorithm dynamically adjusts the state to optimize for speed and efficiency. We explore a method that utilizes entanglement as a dynamic pathway for state transformation, achieving significantly enhanced transfer rates compared to existing techniques. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, introduces key mathematical formulations, and provides a preliminary analysis demonstrating its potential for substantial speedup in complex quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Systems Modeling of Neural Networks with Phase-Space Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of neural networks through the lens of dynamical systems theory and phase-space analysis. Traditional approaches to neural network training often rely on gradient-based methods, which can be sensitive to initial conditions and prone to getting trapped in local minima. By treating neural networks as dynamical systems, we can gain a deeper understanding of their underlying behavior, identify potential instabilities, and develop more robust training strategies. This work introduces a framework for analyzing the state space of a neural network – the phase space – and utilizing techniques from classical mechanics, such as Poincaré sections and Lyapunov exponents, to characterize the network's dynamics. The core contribution is demonstrating how phase-space analysis can reveal previously hidden patterns in neural network behavior, leading to a more informed approach to network design and optimization. Specifically, we explore the concept of a network's "basin of attraction" and how it relates to the network's convergence properties. We present a theoretical model and illustrate the application of this method with a simple, yet illustrative, feedforward neural network. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundational understanding for applying dynamical systems techniques to neural networks, paving the way for improved training algorithms and enhanced network performance.

title: Formal Modeling and Verification of Secure Multi-Party Computation Protocols
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing and verifying secure multi-party computation (SMPC) protocols through formal modeling and interactive theorem proving. We introduce new protocols that prioritize both security and efficiency. The core of our approach lies in representing these protocols as precise logical formulas. This enables automated verification of their correctness and resilience against malicious participants. The methods described here significantly advance the field by offering a rigorous and demonstrable assurance of protocol behavior, moving beyond traditional security proofs relying on assumptions and black-box testing. The key contributions of this work include a formalized representation of SMPC protocols and the application of interactive theorem proving for their verification. This allows for a systematic and exhaustive examination of the protocol's properties, leading to increased confidence in their secure operation. The presented protocols demonstrate improved efficiency compared to existing approaches while maintaining strong security guarantees.

We introduce new protocols that prioritize both security and efficiency. The core of our approach lies in representing these protocols as precise logical formulas. This enables automated verification of their correctness and resilience against malicious participants. The methods described here significantly advance the field by offering a rigorous and demonstrable assurance of protocol behavior, moving beyond traditional security proofs relying on assumptions and black-box testing. The key contributions of this work include a formalized representation of SMPC protocols and the application of interactive theorem proving for their verification. This allows for a systematic and exhaustive examination of the protocol's properties, leading to increased confidence in their secure operation. The presented protocols demonstrate improved efficiency compared to existing approaches while maintaining strong security guarantees.

title: Quantum-Driven Parallel Algorithm Design for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-Driven Parallel Algorithm Design for Complex Systems explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize parallel algorithm design, addressing limitations inherent in traditional approaches. The core mechanism involves employing quantum-inspired algorithms to identify novel parallel patterns, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for algorithm discovery. This paper presents a detailed investigation of this approach, outlining the theoretical foundation, experimental validation, and potential implications for complex system optimization. The focus is on exploring how quantum phenomena can be harnessed to uncover previously unseen parallelism, ultimately leading to more efficient and robust algorithms. This work represents a significant step towards a more profound understanding of parallel computation and a potential shift in the field.

title: 自适应拓扑量子计算的特征因子计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive topology quantum computing feature factor calculation method. Traditional feature factorization methods often rely on static approaches, limiting their precision and hindering optimization. Our proposed method leverages the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust the feature factor during the evolution of quantum systems, enabling precise and tailored calculations. We detail the design of this method, including the simulation framework and the mechanism for topological structure adjustment. The core claim highlights the effectiveness of this approach in achieving accurate feature factor computation and quantum system optimization. This work presents a significant advancement in the field, offering a fundamentally new approach to feature factorization, potentially unlocking new possibilities for quantum algorithm design and optimization.

title: 基于自适应量子算法的非线性概率模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probability modeling leveraging the inherent randomness of quantum computation. We introduce a dynamically adaptive probabilistic model, designed to enhance model precision and improve prediction accuracy through iterative optimization guided by quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum randomness to dynamically adjust probability distributions, enabling the model to adapt to complex environments and achieve superior predictive capabilities. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with this adaptability. This work explores how quantum algorithms can provide a more flexible and robust framework for probabilistic representation and refinement. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy in specific scenarios.

title: Integrasi ABSA dan LDA untuk identifikasi opini publik Kabupaten Pakpak Bharat
abstract: Penelitian ini mengusulkan pendekatan Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) yang mengintegrasikan Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) dan IndoBERT untuk menganalisis opini publik terhadap Kabupaten Pakpak Bharat berdasarkan 4.591 tweet yang dikumpulkan melalui scraping. Data diproses melalui case folding, penghapusan URL dan mention, serta penyaringan stopword yang mempertimbangkan konteks. LDA digunakan untuk membangun taksonomi topik secara otomatis yang terdiri atas tujuh kategori, yang menjadi dasar ekstraksi aspek berbasis aturan menggunakan mekanisme pembobotan kata kunci dengan batasan taksonomi. Aspek dengan data yang tidak memadai digabungkan ke dalam kategori induk yang relevan secara semantik, menghasilkan sembilan kelas aspek akhir. Untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas sentimen, diterapkan strategi random oversampling berbasis threshold, di mana setiap kelas minoritas ditingkatkan jumlahnya hingga nilai minimum antara ukuran kelas mayoritas dan nilai maksimum antara jumlah data saat ini atau 30% dari ukuran kelas mayoritas—sehingga dataset menjadi lebih seimbang dengan total 4.755 sampel tanpa menyamakan seluruh kelas secara penuh. Klasifikasi sentimen dilakukan menggunakan arsitektur multitask IndoBERT dengan dua classification head, di mana head aspek dilatih secara bersamaan menggunakan Focal Loss sebagai komponen pendukung untuk memperkuat representasi bersama, sementara label aspek akhir ditentukan melalui mekanisme berbasis aturan tersebut. Tiga aspek dengan volume pembahasan tertinggi adalah Keamanan (1.354 data), Sosial (1.313 data), dan Pariwisata (794 data). Model klasifikasi sentimen menunjukkan performa yang baik, dengan akurasi 85,59%, presisi 84%, recall 86%, dan F1-score 85%. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa integrasi LDA, ekstraksi berbasis aturan, dan IndoBERT efektif dalam memetakan persepsi publik secara granular, serta memberikan wawasan yang dapat ditindaklanjuti bagi evaluasi pemerintah daerah.

title: Zero-Shot Annotation by Large Language Model with Serial Correction of Mixed Label Corruption for Weakly Supervised Financial News Classification
abstract: Multi-label classification of financial news is frequently affected by incomplete and noisy annotations, while obtaining expert-curated labels at scale is prohibitively expensive. This study proposes a weakly supervised classification framework that combines large language model (LLM) zero-shot annotation with a serial label-correction strategy. The framework first uses an LLM to generate initial weak labels and then refines them through a two-stage Correct→Clean procedure that recovers missing labels via centrality-weighted graph propagation before suppressing label noise. Systematic experiments on a financial subset of Reuters-21578 show that, under an extreme mixed-corruption setting with 80% missing labels and 15% noise labels, Correct→Clean increases the Micro-F1 from 0 to 0.6748. In an end-to-end evaluation, the proposed framework achieves a Micro-F1 of 0.8882 with reduced-dimensional features, recovering 88.69% of the performance gap to fully supervised learning. Additional experiments on the RCV1 Topics and AAPD datasets confirm that the advantage of Correct→Clean is consistently reproduced across domains and dataset sizes. These findings demonstrate that coupling LLM-generated annotations with ordered label correction offers an effective means of addressing the joint effects of missing and noisy labels, providing a promising approach to financial text classification when expert annotations are scarce.

title: Distributed planning and control for UAV swarms under obstacle avoidance and time constraints
abstract: To address the distributed planning and control requirements of UAV swarms operating in cluttered environments under coupled obstacle-avoidance and time-constrained arrival objectives, a swarm planning and control method based on distributed reinforcement learning is proposed in this paper. Considering information available from onboard sensors, static obstacles are represented using a fixed-memory 3D occupancy voxel map, and compact environmental features are extracted via 3D ray casting. Meanwhile, inter-agent interactions are encoded by a neighbor bounding-box matrix, enabling distributed decision-making relying only on local observations. On the algorithmic side, the proposed method adopts the multi-agent proximal policy optimization(MAPPO) framework and incorporates an attention mechanism in the value network to explicitly model multi-agent relations. To handle bounded action outputs, the policy is parameterized by a Beta distribution, and training efficiency and generalization are enhanced through parallel sampling and transfer training. Experiments are conducted on a quadrotor swarm simulation platform built in Gazebo. Compared with training without transfer learning, the success rates are improved, demonstrating more pronounced advantages in densely cluttered scenarios. In comparative studies, EGO-Swarm and ViGO achieve collision-free probabilities of 98.15% and 90.05%, while their planning success rates with transfer learning are 75.06% and 74.89%, respectively. Trajectory evaluations further indicate that the proposed method enables collision-free multi-agent arrivals within the specified time limit, exhibiting stable cooperative avoidance and reliable satisfaction of time constraints.

title: ObGynLongBench: Revealing the Evidence-to-EHR Gap in Longitudinal EHR Decision-Making
abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) to personalized medical assistants has garnered growing interest. However, existing medical benchmarks largely rely on static question answering with pre-selected evidence, leaving unclear whether LLMs can make reliable clinical decisions from real longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs). To bridge this gap, we introduce ObGynLongBench, a rule-grounded long-context EHR benchmark for obstetric and gynecologic decision-making, comprising 1,500 clinical decision-point cases from 976 real pregnancy EHR histories and traceable rules. Each case is anchored to a patient, a pregnancy-timeline point, and a pre-decision information boundary, enabling Evidence-only, Visit-level EHR, and History-level EHR evaluation. Evaluating 17 LLMs reveals a substantial Evidence-to-EHR Gap: models perform well when evidence is directly provided, but accuracy drops when evidence must be extracted from same-day records or full pre-decision EHR histories. Further analyses identify evidence utilization as a key bottleneck: performance decreases with longer EHR contexts and more complex evidence requirements, and earlier failures often predict later failures within the same patient history. Finally, active-search agents perform best among EHR access strategies, highlighting patient-specific evidence utilization as a central challenge for reliable personalized medical assistants. Resources are available at https://github.com/xiangjun2003/ObgynLongbench.

title: Quality Metrics for LLM-Generated Asset Administration Shells: A Perturbation-Based Evaluation Approach
abstract: The rapid digital transformation of manufacturing, often referred to as Industry 4.0, relies on seamless interoperability between physical and software assets. A central enabler is the Asset Administration Shell (AAS), a standardized digital representation of such assets. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable the generation of AAS submodels from unstructured sources such as product datasheets but raise challenges for quality assurance. In particular, unexpected errors, the lack of ground truth references, and the absence of standardized quality metrics hinder reliable adoption. In this work, we evaluate quality metrics for AI-generated AAS using a perturbation-based evaluation framework. By systematically degrading AAS generation along multiple dimensions, we assess how well different metrics reflect quality changes. Based on a dataset of 200 products from multiple manufacturers, we generate 6,400 AAS instances using GPT-4o-mini, Qwen3, and DeepSeek-R1. Our results show that metrics based on exact matching of property names and similarity-based soft matching of property values, in particular value-based recall and name-based F1 score, provide the most reliable indicators of quality degradation. Furthermore, we quantify the impact of different perturbation types and analyze differences across model families and product segments. These findings support the selection of suitable metrics, the tuning of LLM-based pipelines, and the integration of AI-generated AAS into industrial applications.

title: From NISQ to Fault-Tolerance: Applications and Algorithmic Benchmarks for Spin Qubits
abstract: Motivated by recent breakthroughs in the development of spin-based quantum processing units based on exchange-only (EO) spin qubits, we provide a roadmap for the implementation of quantum algorithms on the EO platform, ranging from the NISQ to the fault-tolerant era. To provide an algorithm-driven perspective on the scaling of quantum chips, we consider a range of applications targeting different stages of hardware maturity and formulate requirements for a successful realization. We show that the compilation method Parity Twine perfectly complements the hardware's capabilities to perform tasks such as the quantum Fourier transform or QAOA. Furthermore, we describe an error detection technique native to Parity Twine, which EO qubits can leverage in a unique and advantageous way to improve algorithm performance. Finally, since both near-term algorithmic benchmarks and a long-term perspective can be found in digital quantum simulation, we specifically discuss the fermionic fast Fourier transform and the simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models. The latter is explicitly discussed in the context of quantum error correction and a partially fault-tolerant realization. By providing detailed resource estimates and identifying scaling bottlenecks on each level, our work offers a quantitative perspective on EO-based quantum computing and will inform future hardware design choices.

title: AstraMoE-SR: Trajectory-Guided Diffusion for Blind Satellite Jitter Deblurring and Super-Resolution
abstract: Pushbroom satellite imaging couples limited spatial resolution with platform attitude instability. Platform jitter produces spatially varying motion blur because each scan line is acquired under a different instantaneous attitude, while perspective geometry causes the same perturbation to induce different pixel displacements across the field of view. Existing blind restoration methods that assume a spatially invariant kernel and satellite jitter correction methods that rely on auxiliary observations are therefore not directly applicable. We present AstraMoE-SR, a single-image framework that jointly restores motion blur and spatial resolution without auxiliary measurements. Rather than estimating a blur kernel, we infer how the camera moved by reparameterizing degradation as a local exposure trajectory under pushbroom geometry. A conditional diffusion model estimates the trajectory distribution, mitigating the over-smoothing of high-frequency jitter by deterministic point estimation. The predicted trajectory conditions a pretrained latent diffusion backbone through trajectory-guided geometric alignment and spatially adaptive reconstruction. We further show that the remaining point-wise trajectory error is consistent with intrinsic jitter-phase ambiguity that is not resolved by increasing estimator capacity. On all 1,411 DOTA-v1.0 images degraded using our physically motivated forward model, AstraMoE-SR is the only evaluated method to outperform the no-restoration baseline across every fidelity metric, improving on StableSR by 0.64 dB PSNR, 15.2% LPIPS, and 0.091 DINO feature similarity. Reconstructions conditioned on predicted trajectories differ negligibly from those using ground-truth trajectories, indicating that the estimates retain the degradation information required for effective restoration.

title: PENINGKATAN PEMAHAMAN TENTANG EXPERT SYSTEM BAGI SISWA DAN GURU SMK BINTANG NUSANTARA
abstract: This community service program aims to improve the understanding and skills of students and teachers at SMK Bintang Nusantara regarding expert systems through socialization, practical workshops, and training. The program was motivated by students' low basic knowledge and practical experience of expert systems, as well as teachers' limited capacity to deliver applicable information technology materials. The program was implemented using the Experiential Learning approach through an initial needs survey, module development, theory sessions, hands-on prototyping of expert systems using open-source software (ES-Builder) with a computer hardware damage diagnosis case study, and mentoring. Evaluation was conducted through pre-test, post-test, project assessment, and satisfaction questionnaires involving 30 participants (25 students and 5 teachers). The results showed a significant increase in participants' average comprehension scores from 45.2 (pre-test) to 82.7 (post-test), with a gain score of 83%. Eighty percent of participant groups successfully built functional expert system prototypes, and 85% of grade XII students expressed interest in using the expert systems theme for their Competency Test (UKK) projects. The program also produced a reusable teaching module and enhanced teachers' capacity to integrate rule-based artificial intelligence materials into the curriculum. Thus, this program contributes to narrowing the technology competency gap between vocational school graduates and the needs of the business and industrial sectors (DUDI).

title: Dimension Uncertainty and Quantum Information Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to address the fundamental challenge of dimensionality in complex systems. We propose a novel algorithm, "Dimension Mapping," which utilizes a concept of "Entanglement Dimension Channels" to model high-dimensional spaces non-linearly, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum system control and prediction. The core mechanism centers around establishing a dynamic connection between high-dimensional quantum states through entangled channels, effectively bypassing the limitations of classical simulation. The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the algorithm's capabilities in predicting and influencing transient quantum behavior. We argue that this approach represents a significant step towards a more robust and versatile framework for quantum information processing.

title: Self-Similar Geometry Quantum Entanglement Models
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-similar geometric models based on quantum entanglement to explore the impact of entanglement on geometric structure and identify potential applications in quantum computing and quantum information. Traditional geometric models often lack a direct consideration of quantum entanglement. This work proposes a novel theoretical framework leveraging quantum entanglement to simulate geometric evolution, offering a pathway to uncover novel quantum computational and information processing possibilities. We outline the core mechanism of this model, detailing the simulation process and the expected impact of entanglement. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this research for both quantum computing and quantum information.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm design leveraging the power of quantum strings. We explore the potential of quantum strings to facilitate the implementation of complex non-linear operations, aiming to enhance algorithmic efficiency. The core mechanism centers around converting traditional non-linear operations into quantum manipulations, capitalizing on the unique quantum properties of strings. We detail the design principles, mathematical underpinnings, and potential benefits of this approach compared to conventional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for research in this area.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Simulation with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos simulation aims to overcome limitations of classical simulations, particularly in modeling complex and unpredictable dynamics. This paper explores a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement and adaptive thresholds to create highly complex and dynamic chaos systems. We propose a method for representing chaotic state by utilizing quantum superposition and dynamically adjusting thresholds to facilitate the evolution of the system. The development of this technique offers the potential for simulating systems with unprecedented levels of complexity and unpredictability, pushing the boundaries of chaos research. The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance the representation of the chaotic state, leading to a more robust and nuanced simulation. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical framework, and the resulting experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.
